- [USER] User expressed interest in notable scientific prizes and the nomination or winning process.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Nobel Prize is awarded annually in categories including physics, chemistry, medicine or physiology, literature, and peace; nominations must come from qualified individuals or organizations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Fields Medal is awarded every four years to mathematicians under 40 for significant contributions; candidates are nominated by a committee of experts from the International Mathematical Union.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Breakthrough Prize, first awarded in 2013, recognizes achievements in life sciences, fundamental physics, and mathematics; nominees are evaluated by a board of advisors.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award is awarded annually to scientists for significant contributions to clinical medicine; nominees are selected by a committee from the Lasker Foundation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Turing Award is awarded annually to computer scientists for significant contributions; nominees are evaluated by a committee from the Association for Computing Machinery.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nomination and selection processes for scientific prizes vary; some require nominations from qualified individuals or organizations, while others have a closed selection process.
- [USER] User found it fascinating that there are many different scientific prizes.
- [USER] User inquired about recent breakthroughs that have won scientific prizes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020 for CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] David Baker won the Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences 2021 for developing new computational methods for designing proteins.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Caucher Birkar won the Fields Medal 2018 for contributions to algebraic geometry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Gladstone Institutes scientists won the Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award 2019 for CAR T-cell therapy development.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Alfred Aho and Jeffrey Ullman won the Turing Award 2020 for their work on compiler theory.
